title: Assay certificate
description:
A laboratory job: the batch of samples one lab analysed and reported together, under one certificate number, on one date. The chain-of-custody anchor a value traces back to.

One laboratory job: who analysed what, when, and in what state.

GENERATED from the normative OpenAPI document (`spec/openapi.yaml`) — do not edit by hand; run `python scripts/regenerate.py`. The OpenAPI document is normative for the wire; this file is the same contract for one record type, readable on its own.

project.description: The project this certificate belongs to, as an identity object rather than a bare id, so a reference stays meaningful across exports.

laboratory.description: The laboratory that issued this certificate, as an identity object. Null when the record does not name one.

analysis_date.description: The date the laboratory reported this certificate.

date_preliminary.description: The date the preliminary report was received, when this record began as one. Null for a certificate that arrived finalized.

status.description:
The state of this certificate record. `preliminary` — a final report is still expected and will replace these values in place; the numbers are usable but not yet the reported result. `finalized` — the reported result. `unverified` — the VALUES are the operator's real numbers, but this certificate record was reconstructed because the source data named no usable certificate; anything that reports or signs off on assay data should be able to exclude these.

* `preliminary` - Preliminary
* `finalized` - Finalized
* `unverified` - Unverified (no certificate in source)

batch_number.description: The laboratory's own batch number for this job, where the lab reports one. QC insertion rates are usually quoted per batch.

weight_units.description:
The units the sample weights on this job were reported in.

* `kg` - kilograms
* `g` - grams
* `lb` - pounds
* `oz` - ounces

alt_certificate_numbers.description: Other laboratory certificate numbers for the SAME job, when a lab split one job across several numbers on the same samples. Match a number you read on a report against `name` OR any entry here.

methods.description: The analytical methods reported on this certificate, as identity objects. The same method may appear on many certificates.

result_count.description: How many assay rows this certificate produced. A zero is INFORMATION, not an error: an intentionally empty placeholder certificate is a legitimate record to hold.

qaqc_status.description: The QAQC review verdict on this certificate. `rejected`: its results are withheld from analysis (each assay and QC sample is returned flagged `excluded` only when you ask with `include_excluded=true`). `pending`: review not finished — on a project that requires approval, its results are withheld until it is. `approved` / `conditional`: results are in use. `none`: no review recorded. This is geoDB's verdict; report it, do not recompute it.

superseded_by.description: The re-assay certificate that REPLACED this one, or null. A superseded certificate's results are withheld; the live values are on the certificate named here.

supersedes.description: The earlier certificates this one replaced as their re-assay (empty when it replaced none).

source_type.description:
`lab` — a laboratory job. `field_xrf` — a portable-XRF reading session: field guidance, never a reportable grade. Field-XRF results are left out of geoDB's lab analytics, QC verdicts and intercepts, and never enter a combined value. Read them with `/api/v2/field-xrf/`.

* `lab` - Laboratory
* `field_xrf` - Field XRF

notes.description: Free-text notes on this certificate (as written by the user or through the records endpoint).

in_trash.description: Present (true) only on a record in the Trash, returned because the read sent `include_trashed=true`. Restore it (its `trash.restore` request) rather than creating its twin.

trash.description: Present only on an `in_trash` row: how to bring it back. `audit_batch_id` is the removal that put it in the Trash (null when it was removed without a batch record: then `note` says to use the web Trash); `batch_records` counts, by record type, everything that one removal took (this record included) and `other_records_in_batch` how many besides it; `restore` is the records request that restores that removal, as a dry run. A restore brings back the WHOLE removal: show the user the dry run's `restoring` (every record it brings back) before sending it with `dry_run: false`.

project_id.description: The project this record is in (a credential may read several; GET /api/v2/grant-context/ names them).
